summary: Pass. The audit covers 2fdb8f8..ff4e009 at HEAD ff4e009, current. The two earlier blockers are fixed with real failing-first tests. First, the token log (Review A 2fdb8f8, tasks 4.13w/x): read_tokens of both runners now reads the real step_finish event with part.tokens and keeps the old step-finish shape working (review-run.sh:144-186, judge-run.sh:105-146). A node proof on the real stream shape gives all zeros at the pre-fix code and the correct sums at HEAD, so the W1 to W3, WJ1, and WJ2 tests fail first. Second, the queue decoder (Review B 2fdb8f8, tasks 4.13u/v): readFindings calls decodeAnswerText before the fence parse (adjudicate.ts:223-269), the two TypeScript decoders are byte-identical (diff prints IDENTICAL), and a node proof gives null at the pre-fix code and the findings at HEAD, so the 4.13u cases fail first. The record schema for the pilot token report (Q1) is complete: each pass record and each probe record holds tokens with input, output, reasoning, cache_read, cache_write, and total, plus tokens_complete, and each diff entry holds its own tokens (review-run.sh:662-684, 827-840; spec D13 Tokens). The judge run record holds the same fields per group (WJ2). The flow from stored output to score file works end to end: the stored event stream decodes the same in all three readers (decode-parity P1 to P3), the queue feeds the judges, apply writes the flat verdicts map, and review-score --verdicts counts false claims and real defects. The drivers keep their contract: the night driver reads state from the newest pass record glob, which matches the runner derivation byte for byte (night-4.11.sh:213-218 vs review-run.sh:398, 402, 584), and the probe driver keeps its one-line refusal and reachable shapes. read_tokens is byte-identical between the runners (diff prints IDENTICAL). All ten gate files pass one file at a time, fakes only: review-run 68 pass 0 fail, judge-run 39, decode-parity 3, adjudicate 23, review-score 27, quota 30, credential-provider 22, adversarial-p4-runner 14, adversarial-p4b 12, seed-messages 17. No fake or server process of this audit stayed behind after any run. Three Nits stay open and none blocks the phase.
nonblocking_findings: N1 [Nit] review-c: The orphan guard of review-run.test.ts can fail a clean run. My first run passed all 68 tests but the guard flagged two processes of the run's own fixture (a timeout wrapper and its fake call, review-run.test.ts:364-367), and the guard also matches any foreign line that holds 'mg-', so a concurrent session trips it too. The clean re-run in a quiet period gave 68 pass, 0 fail. Rationale: the gate is not deterministic under load, and a later round can lose time to the same flake. Scope the filter to the fixture tag or add a settle wait.

N2 [Nit] review-c: The plan rows 4.12 and 4.13 still name 'the token log of the step-finish events' (measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md:1913, 1959). The code now reads two shapes and rows 4.13w and 4.13x record the change. Rationale: the older row text understates the token contract that the code meets.

N3 [Nit] review-c: read_tokens skips a step_finish event whose part holds no tokens object, instead of marking the call incomplete (review-run.sh:162-170). A call that mixes one full token event and one tokens-less step_finish event keeps tokens_complete true. The real bundle writes tokens on every step_finish event, and a call with no token event at all still sets the flag false, so the spec line of D13 holds. Rationale: one edge of the completeness flag stays unpinned.
evidence: Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD gives ff4e0093a9e6d1d62c8d8ededf2e738cdc152a45, the audited head, current at the start and at the end of the gates. phase_base_sha 57baaaa364f968a2f44c6e14eb96f8a9d68beebf and role_base_sha 2fdb8f8f5be14c395f4883fcc2a143d1bf7e9d41 match the brief. git status shows no modification of any audited file; the range 2fdb8f8..ff4e009 touches the five test files, the fake, adjudicate.ts, judge-run.sh, review-run.sh, review-score.ts, and plan.md.

Blocker 1 fixed, the token log: read_tokens at review-run.sh:144-186 and judge-run.sh:105-146 reads event.type step-finish with event.tokens and event.type step_finish with part.tokens. Node proof on the real stream shape {type:step_finish, part:{type:step-finish, tokens:{input:10, output:20, reasoning:5, cache:{read:100, write:7}}}}: the pre-fix block of 2fdb8f8 prints 0 0 0 0 0 0 and the HEAD block prints 10 20 5 100 7 1. The old fake shape keeps working in both. A non-number token field gives the sums with flag 0. So W1, W2, W3, WJ1, and WJ2, which assert the real sums and tokens_complete true, fail at the Red base and pass at HEAD. The fake prints the real shapes only through the new token_stream field, and the old tokens field stays, so T1, T2, J7, and J8 stay green.

Blocker 2 fixed, the queue decoder: readFindings at adjudicate.ts:223-269 calls decodeAnswerText before the fence parse. Node proof with the fence split over two text events at a line boundary: the pre-fix readFindings of 2fdb8f8 prints null and the HEAD readFindings prints the findings; plain text still parses. So the 4.13u stream cases fail at the Red base and pass at HEAD. diff of review-score.ts:233-261 against adjudicate.ts:223-251 prints IDENTICAL, and the parity test drives all three readers through their public paths (decode-parity.test.ts:590-634).

Record schema for the pilot token report Q1: the pass record holds set_id, route, pass, date, state, diffs with id and tokens, outputs, errors, tokens with total, and tokens_complete (review-run.sh:662-684), and holds no complete field and no rank field (review-run.sh:44-45). The probe record holds set_id, route, diff, date, state, tokens with total, and tokens_complete (review-run.sh:817-840). TOKENS_ALL starts 1 and any incomplete call, transport error, region error, or credential stop sets it 0 (review-run.sh:407, 1005-1057). Spec D13 Tokens at measure/tracks/model_guide/spec.md:680-684 names the same keys.

Flow from stored output to score file: review-run.sh stores the unchanged stdout of the format json call (review-run.sh:1041). The three readers decode the same stream (decode-parity P1, P2, P3). The queue groups the findings by diff, file, and line window (adjudicate.ts:312-406). judge-run.sh writes the flat verdict map judge-a.json and judge-b.json, and its run record holds the group tokens (WJ2). apply writes verdicts.json, the flat map that review-score --verdicts reads (adjudicate.ts:409-440, review-score.ts:497-510). The scorer counts false claims and real defects per verdict (review-score.ts:344-403) and writes the score file fields of spec D13.

Driver contract, read only: the night driver derives run_slug and route_tag the same way as the runner and reads state from the newest pass record of the glob (night-4.11.sh:213-228 vs review-run.sh:398, 402, 584). The probe driver records a refusal as one review-run: line with exit 2 and a pass as one reachable line (probe-4.10.sh:139-146). The range changes no refusal line and no driver-facing shape: W2 asserts the unchanged probe line, and review-run.test.ts pins the refusal exits.
Route parity: diff of the read_tokens block of both runners prints IDENTICAL, and the two TypeScript decoders are byte-identical. The guard functions are untouched by the range.

Plan claim check: row 4.13x names review-run 68 pass 0 fail, judge-run 39, decode-parity 3, adjudicate 23, review-score 27, and adversarial-p4b 12; my clean runs match all six counts. Row 4.13u names the Red failure 2 failed 21 passed (23); the node proof of the pre-fix null supports it. Row 4.13v names no test file changed in the Green commit; git diff --stat bc0391f confirms. Row 4.13x Green commit f88f9b6 changes the two runners only.

Process hygiene: after each gate file, pgrep -af 'fake-opencod[e]|quota-serve[r]' showed nothing of this audit. The first review-run run failed only its own orphan guard while a concurrent session ran judge gates; the clean re-run in a quiet period exited 0.
